newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian market investigates fake Surgut shares.
newsitem.headline: Russian market investigates fake Surgut shares.

text.p: Russian equities market participants and regulators are investigating illicit sales of ordinary and preferred shares in OAO Surgutneftegaz one of Russia's three biggest oil companies.
The shares, whose volume was estimated by one trader at $8.5 million had not reached clients, but many large Russian brokers had suffered, they said.
Brokers had traded the shares on the basis of forged receipts from Surgutneftegaz's share registrar.
Dealers said the trades based on the forgery had been possible because of the length of time it took Surgutneftegaz's share registrar Surgutinvestneft to re-register shares.

"If Surgut has transferred its register to the Central Moscow Depositary the incident would have been impossible. There you get a receipt within two days, and in Surgut you get it within two weeks," said Creditanstalt-Grant chief trader Andrei Galperin.
But Surgutinvestneft said it was not to blame.

"We heard about two days ago that faked receipts dated February 28 had appeared," Surgutinvestneft economist Nina Grekhova said. "Whoever is interested in getting a confirmation can write or call us, we shall clear up everything."
The Federal Commission for the Securities Market, Russia's main market watchdog, will join the investigation if it receives written complaints, commission spokesman Yuri Kotler said.
If a crime is found to have been committed, the violator could be imprisoned for 15 years under a law punishing securities forgery, he said.
The national brokers association NAUFOR played down the latest incident.
"I do not think it should be taken as something extraordinary: the risk is incorporated into the market, everyone lives with it, everyone fears it," NAUFOR president Dmitry Ponomaryov told Reuters.
Surgutneftegaz ordinaries have risen to $0.863 from $0.810 at Friday's close and preferred to $0.6000 from $0.560.
But traders said the incident was nearly settled and share prices were little changed on Thursday.

"On the one hand, the incident demonstrates how high the risks are on our market. On the other hand, there is some stability of the market. Big operators have assumed the risks themselves and you can be sure clients will not have losses," Galperin said.
Ponomaryov said that NAUFOR had disconnected a small broker from the Russian Trading System equities market operated by NAUFOR after traders' complaints about the incident.

The price rise on high volumes in Surgut shares between Monday and Wednesday was due to deals with the broker, traders said. Many big operators found themselves in short positions and had to close the deals urgently.
The forgeries are the latest in a series of scandals affecting Surgutneftegaz shares.
Last October parent Surgut Holding raised its stake in Surgutneftegaz by acquiring an entire new issue, diluting the stakes of other shareholders who had not been aware of the issue.
It subsequently acknowledged this was wrong and agreed to give existing shareholders the right to buy extra shares, and pay more for the share issue it had taken up.
